records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] that stringify to the same garbage literal key, so one overwrites the other and expiry validation is effectively absent
records.rationale: The diff shows `minimumTokenResponseSchema` with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts. Zod schemas have no meaningful toString override, so both computed keys stringify identically (e.g. '[object Object]'), one property overwrites the other, and the intended expiry/extra-property validation never happens. Verifiable from the diff.

records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService performs token refresh plus prisma.credential.update unconditionally on every connection creation with no expiry check, adding a network round-trip and DB write per operation and risking rate limiting
records.rationale: The diff shows new code in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts that performs a fetch to login.salesforce.com and a prisma.credential.update inside the connection-creation path (before 'return new jsforce.Connection'), with no expiry/caching check visible. This is a real, specific performance/rate-limit risk introduced by the change: every service instantiation now triggers a network round-trip and a DB write. It is not a correctness defect per se (the token is still valid), so it is a substantive non-bug concern grounded in the diff.

records.issue_text: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse in app-credential.ts are unguarded, so a bad encryption key or non-JSON plaintext causes an unhandled 500
records.rationale: The diff shows `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` in app-credential.ts with no try/catch; a wrong key or non-JSON plaintext will throw an unhandled exception, producing a 500 instead of a handled error response. This is a real, verifiable robustness/correctness gap in newly added code (the zod `.parse` above is similarly unguarded, corroborating the pattern).
